adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept `(event, credentialId)` and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. GoogleCalendarService uses `credentialId` to select the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` keeps `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and explicitly selects only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). Separately, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and creates events per destination/credential (e.g., collective team events push multiple destination calendars). Because Lark always uses the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is being used, creating an event for a non-main host credential will attempt to insert into the main host’s calendar ID, which can fail due to access/token mismatch. This is a concrete correctness issue grounded in the shown changes.
